finding.claim: Unvalidated iconUrl is stored from update() and later fetched by the nightly sync() job via HttpClient GET, enabling blind server-side requests to arbitrary http/https hosts (internal/RFC-1918/metadata). Severity MEDIUM: response body is discarded, not returned to the attacker.
finding.source: Profile.java:11 update(String webhook, String icon) — icon parameter (PUT /profile per comment)

trace.note: this.iconUrl = icon; stored with no validation
URI.create(iconUrl) builds request URI from stored value
c.send GET dispatches server-side request, body discarded via ofByteArray

finding.guards_checked: update() validates only webhook (line 12 regex), not icon; sync() performs no re-validation before fetch; scheme limited to http/https by java.net.http; redirect following depends on injected HttpClient config (default NEVER) — not verifiable in repo; PUT /profile auth not in repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. update() validates only webhook at src/Profile.java:12-14; icon is stored unchecked at :16 and passed straight to URI.create at :23-24 with no host, scheme, or allowlist check. The java.net.http scheme restriction and default no-redirect config are not closing guards under the rubric.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: icon enters update() at src/Profile.java:11, is stored unvalidated at :16, and is fetched via GET in sync() at :23-24. The source is the request parameter of PUT /profile (src/Profile.java:10), which is user-supplied by design, so it is attacker-controlled unless the endpoint's auth restricts it to admins; that auth lives outside this repo and is the one caveat to the verdict.
